title: Kobalos Linux Trojan Investigation Exercise
description: Investigate a complex Linux threat targeting high performance computing infrastructure named Kobalos.
outcomes: Analyze the provided sandbox environment, MISP event, and security profile to identify and investigate the Kobalos Linux Trojan.
Identify the location where the Kobalos payload has been dropped on the target host.
Investigate the target host for signs of this persistence mechanism.
Identify the IP address of the Command & Control server used by the Kobalos Linux Trojan.

levels.title: Introduction to the Kobalos Linux Trojan Investigation
levels.content: Welcome to the Kobalos Linux Trojan Investigation exercise. Your mission is to investigate a complex Linux threat targeting high performance computing infrastructure named Kobalos. We have provided you with a sandbox environment and MISP event containing indicators of compromise (IOCs) related to this malware.

levels.title: Accessing the Sandbox Environment
levels.cloud_content: Use the provided credentials to connect to the target host via SSH.
levels.local_content: The target host is running Ubuntu and has been compromised by the Kobalos Linux Trojan. You will use SSH to access the target host with the provided credentials.

levels.title: Identify Kobalos Payload Drop Location
levels.content:
ls -la /tmp
Find the Kobalos payload drop location.
levels.solution: The Kobalos payload is dropped in the /tmp directory. Look for files with suspicious names related to the Kobalos Trojan, such as /tmp/.installer.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Look for files with suspicious names related to the Kobalos Trojan in common directories such as /tmp, /var/tmp, or /home/user/.

levels.title: Investigate Kobalos Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
strings /etc/ld.so.preload | grep LD_PRELOAD
Investigate the target host for signs of this persistence mechanism.
levels.solution: The Kobalos Linux Trojan is known for using various persistence mechanisms, one common technique is to use LD_PRELOAD to inject malicious code into legitimate processes. Check for the presence of LD_PRELOAD strings in the /etc/ld.so.preload file.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.content: Check for the presence of LD_PRELOAD strings in the /etc/ld.so.preload file.

levels.title: Identify Kobalos C2 Communication
levels.content:
netstat -an | grep 7070
Identify the IP address of the Command & Control server used by the Kobalos Linux Trojan.
levels.solution: The Kobalos Linux Trojan is known to communicate with its Command & Control server over a specific port. Investigate the target host for signs of this communication.

hints.title: Hint 3
hints.content: Look for open network connections on port 7070 using the `netstat` command.
